description: File tree operations (create, rename, delete, drag-drop reorder, sort options) and file management matching Obsidian's file explorer behavior
steps: 1. Add file/folder CRUD operations to the vault store (src/store/vault-store.ts): createFile(parentFolderId, name), createFolder(parentFolderId, name), renameNode(fileId, newName), deleteNode(fileId). For demo vault: mutate the in-memory manifest. For FSA vaults: use the File System Access API (writeFileText, rename via copy+delete, remove). After any CRUD op, update the manifest and pathIndex.

2. In src/components/vault/FileTree.tsx, replace the alert() stubs in the context menu with working implementations: 'New Note' creates a new .md file in the selected folder (or root), prompts for a name via an inline input field that appears in the tree. 'New Folder' similarly creates a folder. 'Rename' turns the node's label into an editable input (inline rename like Obsidian). 'Delete' shows a confirmation dialog using AlertDialog from shadcn, then removes the file.

3. Add drag-and-drop reordering to the file tree. Use HTML5 drag events (not @dnd-kit, to keep it simple). Allow dragging files/folders to reorder within a folder or move between folders. Show drop indicators (line above/below for reorder, highlight for move-into-folder). Update the manifest's childIds ordering after drop.

4. Add a 'Sort by' option to the file tree header (above the tree): options for 'Name (A-Z)', 'Name (Z-A)', 'Modified (newest)', 'Modified (oldest)', 'Created (newest)'. Store the sort preference in the vault store or a UI state. Apply sorting to childIds when rendering.

5. Add a 'New Note' button (+ icon) to the left sidebar header next to the search toggle. Clicking it creates a new untitled note in the root folder and immediately opens it in the active editor leaf with the title focused for editing.
6. Add keyboard shortcut Ctrl+N for 'New note' (matching Obsidian). Register in use-builtin-commands.ts. The command creates a new note and opens it.

7. Add file tree filtering: a small filter input at the top of the file tree that filters visible nodes as you type (matching Obsidian's file explorer filter). This is separate from the full search panel.
acceptance_criteria: Right-click context menu on a folder shows 'New Note', 'New Folder', 'Rename', 'Delete' and all work
Right-click context menu on a file shows 'Rename', 'Delete', 'Open in new pane' and all work
Ctrl+N creates a new note and opens it for editing
Files can be dragged to reorder within a folder or moved to another folder
Sort options are available and change the tree ordering
Deleting a file that has open tabs closes those tabs
bun run lint passes with zero errors
